metadata.title: Pages and fragments — Gazetta
metadata.description: Page and fragment manifests, routes, translations, custom 404 pages and project layout.

components.name: docs-pages-and-fragments-body
components.content:
> These docs describe Gazetta's `main` branch. The latest release on npm, 0.8.0, is older and works differently in places, and it lacks security fixes made since. To follow these docs, [run Gazetta from `main`](https://github.com/gazetta-studio/gazetta-studio#quick-start). # Pages and fragments Pages define routes; fragments share components between pages. This guide covers their manifests, dynamic routes, translations, custom 404 pages and on-disk layout. For template code, see [Templates](/docs/templates). ## Pages A page is a folder with a `page.json` manifest under the editing target's `pages/` root, which `init` sets to `sites/main/targets/local/pages/`. The route is derived from the folder path - `pages/about/` becomes `/about`, and `pages/home/` is served at `/`: ```json { "template": "page-layout", "content": { "title": "About", "description": "About our company" }, "components": [ "@header", { "name": "about-text", "template": "text-block", "content": { "body": "

We build composable websites.

" } } ] } ``` Inline components live in the page manifest; shared components use fragment references such as `@header`. While `gazetta dev` runs, a new page folder is picked up without a restart. Or create pages in the CMS - click **New page** in the admin UI. ### Dynamic routes Use `[param]` in the folder name - it becomes `:param` in the route: A page at `pages/blog/[slug]/page.json` serves `/blog/:slug`: ```json { "template": "page-layout", "components": [ { "name": "post-body", "template": "text-block", "content": { "body": "

First post.

" } } ] } ``` String entries in `components` must be fragment references starting with `@`; an inline component is an object with `name`, `template` and `content`. In `gazetta dev`, templates receive the captured route params. Published pages are pre-rendered: `serve` and the worker match the route pattern but do not re-run templates with each request's params. Do not rely on request-time `params` to generate published content. A complete typed template for the dev-server example: ```ts import type { TemplateFunction } from 'gazetta' import { z } from 'zod' export const schema = z.object({ title: z.string().optional() }) type Content = z.infer const escapeHtml = (value: string) => value.replace(/[&<>"']/g, char => `&#${char.charCodeAt(0)};`) const template: TemplateFunction = ({ content, params }) => ({ html: `

${escapeHtml(content?.title ?? params?.slug ?? '')}

`, css: '', js: '', }) export default template ``` ## Fragments Fragments are shared components reusable across pages. They live under the editing target's `fragments/` root and are referenced with `@`. For example, `fragments/header/fragment.json`: ```json { "template": "nav", "content": { "brand": "My Site", "links": [ { "label": "Home", "href": "/" }, { "label": "About", "href": "/about" } ] } } ``` Reference in any page with `"@header"`. Update the fragment once and pages using it share the change in `gazetta dev`. Published targets change only when you publish: static targets contain fully assembled pages, while dynamic targets assemble published fragments at request time. See [Targets](/docs/targets#type). ## Custom 404 page `gazetta init` already created a `pages/404/` page. It's served with a 404 status when a route doesn't match, and the URL stays as-is - no redirect. The starter 404 uses the `page-layout` template with just a title and description. To add body content, add inline components in `pages/404/page.json` (a bare string must be a fragment reference starting with `@`, and `init` creates only a `@header` fragment): ```json { "template": "page-layout", "content": { "title": "Page Not Found", "description": "The page you're looking for doesn't exist." }, "components": [ { "name": "message", "template": "text-block", "content": { "body": "

Nothing here. Back to the homepage.

" } } ] } ``` Works with `gazetta dev`, `gazetta serve` and Cloudflare Workers. Fragments are assembled normally. List the page in `systemPages: ['404']` in `site.config.ts` to exclude it from `sitemap.xml`; `init` sets that up. A page's `metadata.robots: "noindex"` also excludes it from the sitemap. The system-page setting does not itself add a robots meta tag. On a static target, every publish also copies the published 404 page to `404.html` at the target root, which Cloudflare Pages, Netlify and GitHub Pages show for missing paths. Until `pages/404` is published to a target, its `404.html` is a minimal "Page not found" page. ## Translations Store a complete manifest for each locale alongside the default manifest: ```text pages/about/ page.json # default locale page.fr.json # French page.en-gb.json # British English fragments/header/ fragment.json # default locale fragment.fr.json # French ``` Locale filenames use lowercase codes. Each variant has its own `template`, `content` and `components`; it is not a field-level patch over `page.json`. Configure the site's supported locales in `site.config.ts`, for example `locales: { default: 'en', supported: ['en', 'fr'] }`. With that configuration and the default URL-prefix settings, `pages/about/page.json` serves `/about` and `page.fr.json` serves `/fr/about`. The translated home page serves `/fr`. Dynamic routes keep the same folder pattern: `pages/blog/[slug]/page.fr.json` maps to `/fr/blog/:slug`. Targets can narrow their locale set or change the default and prefix settings. For a French page, `@header` uses `fragment.fr.json` when available, then the configured fallback chain, then `fragment.json`. Both pages and fragments remain whole manifests. See [Targets](/docs/targets) for target configuration. ## Indexing localized pages Each locale file (for example `page.fr.json`) is a complete page manifest. Its own `metadata.robots` controls indexing in both rendered HTML and the published sitemap: `"noindex"` excludes that locale URL without excluding the default page, and an omitted `robots` value permits indexing even if the default page is `noindex`. An ordinary publish also corrects a previously published locale's stale indexing flag, even when its content hash has not changed; `--force` is not required. ## Site structure ``` my-project/ package.json admin/ # custom editors + fields (shared across sites) editors/ hero.tsx fields/ brand-color.tsx templates/ # developer-created templates (shared across sites) hero/index.ts nav/index.ts page-layout/index.ts sites/ main/ site.config.ts # site manifest + targets targets/ local/ # the local filesystem target's content root fragments/ # shared components header/fragment.json pages/ # routable pages home/ page.json # all components inline about/ page.json blog/ [slug]/page.json # dynamic route ``` Templates and admin customizations are at the project root, shared across all sites. `site.config.ts` sits at `sites/{name}/`; the pages and fragments a site serves live in its editing target's content root, which `init` sets to `sites/{name}/targets/local/`. --- [Edit this page on GitHub](https://github.com/gazetta-studio/gazetta-studio/edit/main/docs/pages-and-fragments.md)
